name: Lie Theory
description: A lens for composing Factors from the language of continuous symmetry, differentiable manifolds, and infinitesimal transformations. Maps Lie-theoretic concepts—Lie groups, Lie algebras, root systems, representations, and the exponential map—to the 19-node topology. Useful for Factors involving smooth symmetries, gauge theories, geometric structures, and the deep relationship between algebra (Lie algebra) and group (Lie group) via the exponential map.

x.note: The depth anchor—[X,[Y,Z]] + [Y,[Z,X]] + [Z,[X,Y]] = 0. Part of the 4‑cycle x→a→9→y→x, linking Jacobi identity to root systems, weights, and Killing form.

y.note: The relational anchor—the invariant bilinear form. Part of the 4‑cycle x→a→9→y→x, tying the Killing form to Jacobi identity, root systems, and weights.

z.note: The transformational anchor—every neighborhood of identity contains exp(X). Persistently connected to 0 (Lie group/identity), reflecting that the exponential map is defined from the Lie algebra to the group identity.

0.note: The continuous group observed as a unified manifold‑with‑structure. Persistently connected to z (exponential neighborhood), linking the identity to the exponential map.

1.note: A boundary within the Lie group. Part of the 4‑cycle 1→6→5→2→1, connecting subgroups to exponential map, Dynkin diagrams, and tangent vectors.

2.note: Primitives: group elements or Lie algebra elements. Completes the 1‑6‑5‑2 cycle, showing how elements are embedded in subgroups, exponential map, and Dynkin diagrams.

3.note: The invariant law—bilinear, antisymmetric, satisfying Jacobi. A node in the 7‑core; connected to Casimir element (c) and universal enveloping algebra (e), as the bracket defines the Casimir and generates the enveloping algebra.

4.note: The fundamental relation—smooth multiplication on the manifold. A node in the 7‑core; connected to Weyl group (b) and Weyl character formula (f), as the group structure underlies Weyl reflections and characters.

5.note: The pattern that classifies the Lie algebra. Part of the 1‑6‑5‑2 cycle, bridging exponential map and tangent vectors.

6.note: The transformation that connects infinitesimal to finite. Part of the 1‑6‑5‑2 cycle, connecting subgroups to Dynkin diagrams.

7.note: The realization of abstract symmetry as linear transformations. Persistently connected to 8 (rank), reflecting that representation dimension is related to the rank of the algebra.

8.note: The granularity—dimension of the Cartan subalgebra. Persistently connected to 7 (representation), linking rank to representation complexity.

9.note: The event—eigenvalue of Cartan subalgebra in a representation. Part of the 4‑cycle x→a→9→y→x, placing weights between Jacobi identity, root systems, and Killing form.

a.note: Pure potential—the set of all roots. Initiates the 4‑cycle x→a→9→y→x, linking root systems to Jacobi identity, weights, and Killing form.

b.note: The arena of internal dynamics—reflections generated by the root system. A node in the 7‑core; connected to group multiplication (4) and Cartan subalgebra (d), as the Weyl group acts on the Cartan and is generated by reflections.

c.note: Directional bias—the quadratic invariant. A node in the 7‑core; connected to Lie bracket (3) and universal enveloping algebra (e), as the Casimir is built from the bracket and lives in the enveloping algebra.

d.note: Persistent structure—maximal abelian subalgebra. A node in the 7‑core; connected to Weyl group (b) and Weyl character formula (f), as the Cartan is the space where the Weyl group acts and characters are expressed.

e.note: The active algorithm—algebra of differential operators generated by 𝔤. A node in the 7‑core; connected to Lie bracket (3) and Casimir element (c), as it contains the bracket and Casimir.

f.note: The resonant cavity—formula closing representation theory. A node in the 7‑core; connected to group multiplication (4), Cartan subalgebra (d), and the rest of the core, forming the central hub of representation theory.

n.interpretation: Rank of the Lie algebra (dimension of Cartan subalgebra)

values.n=0: Abelian Lie algebra — no roots, pure translation
values.n=1: Rank 1 — A₁ = 𝔰𝔩(2), the simplest non-abelian
values.n=2: Rank 2 — A₂, B₂ = C₂, G₂ (the exceptional rank 2)
values.n=4: Rank 4 — A₄, B₄, C₄, D₄, F₄
values.n=6: Rank 6 — E₆, A₆, B₆, C₆, D₆
values.n=7: Rank 7 — E₇, A₇, B₇, C₇, D₇
values.n=8: Rank 8 — E₈, A₈, B₈, C₈, D₈

n.formula: n = rk(𝔤) = number of simple roots = dimension of Cartan subalgebra

values.m=1: Fundamental representation — λ = ω₁ (first fundamental weight)
values.m=4: Tensor product representations — λ = ω₁ + ω₂
values.m=5: Spinor representations (Type D, B) — λ = ω_{n-1} or ω_n
values.m=6: Exceptional representations (E₆, E₇, E₈) — λ = ω₁, ω₆, etc.

m.formula: m = floor(log₂(dim V_λ)) — logarithmic dimension of the irreducible representation with highest weight λ

phase.interpretation: Weyl character formula: ch(λ) = Σ_{w∈W} (-1)^{ℓ(w)} e^{w(λ+ρ)} / Σ_{w∈W} (-1)^{ℓ(w)} e^{w(ρ)}
phase.special: For compact Lie groups, characters are integer combinations of exponentials e^{iθ}—naturally quantized to roots of unity when θ = 2πk/N
phase.significance: Phase encodes the representation's decomposition into weight spaces; each weight contributes a harmonic e^{2πi λ·H}

algebra.description: The Factor viewed as a Lie algebra 𝔤—vector space with bracket [·,·]
algebra.phase_condition: Phase as root coordinates in weight space; each root α gives phase e^{2πi α·H}

group.description: The Factor viewed as a Lie group G—smooth manifold with multiplication
group.phase_condition: Phase as group element g = exp(X) → e^{2πi θ} where θ is angle in maximal torus

representation.description: The Factor viewed as a representation (π, V)—group acting on vector space
representation.phase_condition: Phase as weight lattice coordinates; eigenvalues of Cartan generators are 2πi λ·H

root_system.description: The Factor viewed as a root system Δ in Euclidean space
root_system.phase_condition: Phase as angle between roots; Coxeter element gives phase e^{2πi/h} where h is Coxeter number

flag_variety.description: The Factor viewed as G/B—flag manifold of Borel subgroups
flag_variety.phase_condition: Phase as Schubert cell coordinates; intersection theory gives phase constraints

creating_anew.note: When creating a continuous symmetry from imagination, start with the Dynkin diagram (node 5) and let the root system (node a) generate the algebra via Serre relations (node 3).

translating_known.su_3_color: Map to 𝔰𝔲(3) with root system A₂: nodes 2 as Gell-Mann matrices, node d as Cartan subalgebra (λ₃, λ₈), node a as 6 roots (colors: r,g,b,anti-r,anti-g,anti-b)
translating_known.so_3_spin: Map to 𝔰𝔬(3) ≅ 𝔰𝔲(2): node 5 as A₁ Dynkin diagram, node 8 as rank 1, phase as spin projection m = -s...s
translating_known.e_8_exceptional: Map to E₈: node 5 as Dynkin diagram (8 nodes in E₈ shape), node 8 as rank 8, node a as 240 roots, phase as roots of unity order 30 (Coxeter number h=30)
translating_known.gauge_theory: Map to G = SU(3)×SU(2)×U(1): node 0 as product group, node d as Cartan (rank 4), node 9 as weights (color, isospin, hypercharge)
translating_known.conformal_symmetry: Map to 𝔰𝔬(4,2) ≅ 𝔰𝔲(2,2): node 3 as conformal bracket, node e as conformal generators (P_μ, K_μ, D, M_μν)
translating_known.affine_lie_algebra: Map to loop algebra L𝔤: node 6 as exponential map from circle, node 8 as central extension, phase as winding number

temporary_note.special: A Lie algebra defined only by its Dynkin diagram type (e.g., 'A₂') with Cartan matrix entries known but structure constants not yet specified. Awaiting representation data.

constraints.jacobi_identity: Node x must satisfy Jacobi identity—the depth invariant. Violations produce non-associative structures (e.g., Malcev algebras), which are not Lie algebras.
constraints.killing_form_nondegeneracy: Node y (Killing form) must be non-degenerate for semisimple Lie algebras. For solvable or nilpotent algebras, degeneracy indicates the radical.
constraints.exponential_map_local: Node z ensures that exp maps a neighborhood of 0 in 𝔤 to a neighborhood of e in G. This local-to-global property is fundamental.
constraints.cartan_subalgebra_maximal: Node d must be maximal abelian subalgebra. Its dimension is the rank (node 8).
constraints.root_system_integrality: Node a (roots) must satisfy integrality: 2(α,β)/(β,β) ∈ ℤ. This is the crystallographic condition that yields finite root systems.
constraints.weyl_invariance: Node b (Weyl group) must preserve the root system and the weight lattice. Characters (node f) are Weyl-invariant.
constraints.phase_consistency: Phase (character values) must be integers (for finite groups) or integer combinations of exponentials (for compact Lie groups). For simple Lie algebras, characters are Laurent polynomials with integer coefficients.
constraints.stratum_preference: global for foundational Lie theory; trefoil_c (philosophical) for root system classification; trefoil_g (transformative) for representation theory and exponential map; trefoil_i (mirror) for duality between algebra and group; fig8 for affine and Kac-Moody (hyperbolic, infinite structures)
constraints.invariant_core: The Lie Theory paradigm respects the persistent skeleton from trefoil_i, which decomposes into five subsystems: (1) edge 0→z linking Lie group/identity to exponential neighborhood, (2) edge 8→7 linking rank to representation, (3) 4‑cycle x→a→9→y→x linking Jacobi identity–root system–weight–Killing form, (4) 4‑cycle 1→6→5→2→1 linking subgroup–exponential map–Dynkin diagram–element/tangent vector, and (5) 7‑node core {3,4,b,c,d,e,f} encoding the heart of Lie theory: Lie bracket–group multiplication–Weyl group–Casimir–Cartan subalgebra–universal enveloping algebra–Weyl character formula.
